title: Paid ads copy set
summary: A set of ready-to-paste ads for Google, Meta or LinkedIn, with several angles to test.
deliverable: Headlines, descriptions and primary text for the chosen platform, grouped by angle, with character counts and a short note on what each angle tests.

spec_fields.label: What are you advertising?
spec_fields.help: The product or offer, price, and any deal.

spec_fields.label: Number of angles to test
spec_fields.help: An angle is one reason to click, such as price or speed.

spec_fields.label: Search terms to target
spec_fields.help: For Google ads.

spec_fields.label: Facts and proof we may use
spec_fields.help: Numbers, prices, quotes, awards. Only these will be quoted.

spec_fields.label: Tone and voice
spec_fields.help: A few words, or paste a sample of your writing.

rubric.text: Each ad follows the length limits and style of its platform.
rubric.pass_rule: Google headlines are 30 characters or fewer and descriptions 90 or fewer; Meta and LinkedIn text respects the stated limits. Counts are shown and correct.

rubric.text: The set tests clearly different reasons to click, not the same line reworded.
rubric.pass_rule: At least three angles are named, and a reader can tell each apart by its main benefit or hook. No two ads share the same opening claim.

rubric.text: Every ad names the offer and asks for the action the buyer chose.
rubric.pass_rule: Each ad group states the offer or benefit and a call to action that matches the goal field.

rubric.text: Nothing is made up: every fact, number, quote or result comes from the brief or files.
rubric.pass_rule: No statistic, price, discount, review, award or guarantee appears unless it is in the brief or the supplied files. Any invented item fails this criterion.

rubric.text: The ads avoid claims that platforms reject or that mislead.
rubric.pass_rule: No guaranteed results, before-and-after claims, lines that call out personal traits (such as 'Are you struggling with...'), all-caps shouting or false urgency.

baseline_prompt: You are a senior paid-media copywriter. Write ad copy for the platform(s) and offer in the brief. Produce three to five distinct angles (for example price, speed, proof, convenience). For each angle give headlines and descriptions or primary text that respect the platform character limits, and show the character count. Match the call to action to the stated goal. Use only facts in the brief; do not invent prices, discounts, reviews or guarantees. Avoid claims that ad policies reject. End with a one-line note on what each angle tests.
not_for: Fake reviews, invented discounts or false scarcity
Ads for regulated offers (loans, investments, medical treatments) that need legal sign-off
Image or video creative, or setting up and running the ad account

sample_briefs.text: I run a plumbing company in Leeds. I want Google search ads for emergency boiler repair. We answer calls within 30 minutes and charge a fixed 89 pounds call-out. Goal is phone calls.
Meta ads for our online yoga studio. 12 pounds a month, first 14 days free, 40 live classes a week. Audience: women 30 to 55 who work from home. Goal: start the free trial.
LinkedIn ads for our payroll software for firms with 20 to 200 staff. We want demo bookings. Our selling points are one-click holiday pay and UK tax filing built in. No customer names allowed.

We are a food bank charity running a Facebook campaign before winter. Goal: monthly donors. One donation of 10 dollars feeds a family for a day, according to our annual report. Keep it respectful, no guilt.
